correctness.rationale: For x dot y = phi(x)y, the Nijenhuis right-hand interior cancels to phi(Nx)y, so applying N gives exactly phi(Nx)N(y), equal to the left side for every endomorphism. The induced product is therefore x dot_N y = (phi composed with N)(x)y. All finite-field counts follow from the surjective linear map End(V) -> V* and standard matrix-rank formulas. The weight-zero Rota-Baxter equation reduces independently to R^2=0, and the square-zero rank count follows by choosing image, kernel, and the quotient-to-image isomorphism. The packaged exhaustive checks agree in every tested small dimension.

originality.rationale: The 2017 source singles out exactly this arbitrary-dimensional family but states only that its weight-zero Rota-Baxter operators are the square-zero maps and hence form a Nijenhuis subclass. The complete Nijenhuis locus is not stated there. The 2026 complete classifications cover only dimensions two and three over the complex numbers; they do not imply the arbitrary-dimensional cancellation theorem or uniform finite-field deformation fibers. Targeted semantic and exact-formula searches found no statement that every endomorphism of the functional family is Nijenhuis.

value.rationale: The family is not an arbitrary construction: it is the arbitrary-dimensional example explicitly selected in the foundational pre-Lie Nijenhuis paper for its Rota-Baxter connection. The complete Nijenhuis answer is maximally rigid in the opposite direction from the square-zero Rota-Baxter condition: every endomorphism works. The induced product remains in the same functional family and is controlled by the simple linear map N -> phi composed with N, producing exact deformation fibers and a uniform finite-field arithmetic description in all dimensions.
